  • Help identify opportunities to maintain or build self-service content: help docs, short-form videos, FAQs, etc.

  • Engage with the Runway community on Discord and other forums

  • Contribute directly to process improvements and automation, including building things yourself when the opportunity is there

  • Triage complex technical issues for escalation to Enterprise support

  • Live troubleshoot within the Runway platform as needed

What you’ll need

  • You're already comfortable in tools like Notion, Slack, Zendesk (or similar), Google Workspace and AI platforms

  • Strong written communication: clear, direct, and thoughtful at volume

  • A learn-by-failing mentality, when you hit something unfamiliar, you have an experimental mindset

  • Natural curiosity about how products work, why users get confused, and what could be done better

  • Comfort managing your own work in a fast-moving environment- high ownership and high autonomy

  • Data driven mindset: you notice patterns and know how to communicate them

  • 1-3 years in customer support, operations, or technical role

  • Expertise and/or interest in the creative space, AI or both

  • Genuine interest in AI, creative tools or both

jobs.descriptionHtml:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.

About the role

*Open to hiring remote across the US — we also have offices in New York, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Paris, and Tel Aviv.

We're looking for a Designer, Growth (Product Marketing) to sit at the intersection of brand, performance marketing, and generative media. This is not a brand systems or campaign concepting role — it's a high-volume, output-driven design role. You'll own the visual execution of paid and performance marketing across video, motion, and static formats, producing assets that are on-brand, well art directed and built to convert. You'll report to the Creative Director of Product Marketing.

Your work will directly shape how people first encounter and engage with Runway's products. That means producing scroll-stopping video ads, designing static and animated assets for paid social and display, and using generative tools — including Runway's own — as a core part of how you work. You'll partner closely with product marketing, growth, and creative teams, and you'll be measured on craft, throughput, and performance.

What you'll do

  • Design and produce high volumes of performance marketing assets across video, motion, and static formats — paid social, display, YouTube and beyond

  • Use Runway to ideate, create and iterate on video and image assets that are on-brand and well art directed — not just technically functional

  • Own the visual execution of ad creative from concept through final delivery, working from briefs or generating your own directions when needed

  • Produce motion graphics and animated ads that communicate product value quickly and compellingly

  • Partner with the Product Marketing and growth team to develop integrated ad concepts where copy and design work together

  • Build and iterate on creative variants for A/B and multivariate testing — adapting formats, hooks and visual treatments based on performance data

  • Maintain a consistent visual language across all performance touchpoints without letting assets feel templated or stale

  • Collaborate with product marketing on go-to-market launches, translating new product capabilities into visual stories that resonate with target audiences

  • Hands-on experience designing for the major paid channels (Meta, YouTube, LinkedIn, etc) with fluency in each platform's native specs, aspect ratios and ad formats, and a real point of view on what works where.

  • Own updates to GTM assets and templates, keeping them current and on-brand across campaigns. Bring hands-on experience building and automating deck design systems, so our presentations stay consistent without manual rework each time.

  • Contribute to a growing library of on-brand design components, motion templates and generative prompting strategies that raise the team's overall output velocity

What you'll need

  • 4+ years of experience in performance marketing design, motion design, or a related role at a tech or consumer company

  • A portfolio that shows range across video ads, motion graphics and static performance creative — with clear evidence of craft and art direction judgment, not just execution

Runway is rapidly building the leading ecosystem of generative models, bringing the best models from AI labs around the world to our users alongside our own. We are looking for an IC to source, activate, and scale relationships across Runway's growing portfolio of model partners. This is a role for someone who wants to own whatever needs owning, take new models from first conversation to launch, and write the playbook where none exists yet. You will work closely across Engineering, Product, Legal, Finance, and Marketing.

What you'll do

  • Own a broad portfolio of model partners end to end, across modalities

  • Track the model landscape relentlessly: spot new labs and releases early and bring the strongest ones to the team as candidates for integration

  • Take new partners from zero to launched: source, structure and negotiate commercial terms, then close with Legal and Finance

  • Be the partner's main point of contact through launch, working closely with our engineering team

  • Build deep, trusted relationships with founders, BD leads and research teams at our partners, and turn those relationships into early access, better terms and joint launches

  • Run the portfolio with rigor: set check-in cadences, monitor relationship health, and spot and escalate risk early

  • Track usage, spend and margin by partner and model, and use that data to decide where to invest, renegotiate or step back

  • Partner with Marketing and our partners on co-marketing for model launches

  • Build the frameworks and tools that let the function scale as the ecosystem grows

What you'll need

  • 5+ years of experience across some combination of partnerships, business development, GTM, consulting, or founding/operating, with a track record of having owned outcomes end to end

  • Experience negotiating commercial agreements, ideally usage-based, API or platform deals

  • Genuine obsession with generative AI: you know the labs, you try new models the day they ship, and you have opinions on what makes one good

  • Demonstrated range: you've done the deal and the integration and the launch

  • High technical aptitude for understanding complex technologies, tools, systems, and issues

  • Strong analytical capabilities, with the ability to turn usage and spend data into a clear recommendation

  • Ability to manage many relationships and priorities at once in a fast-paced environment without dropping threads

  • Clear, concise communication, from a startup founder to a big-lab partnerships team to a Runway engineer in the same day

  • A strong bias towards action and belief that no task is too small for you

  • Highly resourceful, with the ability to create structure and work autonomously amid ambiguity

We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.

About the role

Open to hiring remote across North America and London — we also have offices in NYC, San Francisco, Seattle, and London.

We're building a tool that makes content creation easy and accessible for all types of creatives. Our users love it. Runway has an actively engaged and growing community of passionate artists and creators worldwide. And we're scaling the systems behind our support team so we can keep delivering delightful experiences as that community grows.

We're looking for a Support Systems Engineer who ships production code, not tickets and specs: someone who takes a fix from proposal to merged PR themselves. This role reports directly to the Head of Customer Experience.

What you’ll do

  • Own the AI support agent, our ticketing system and other Support tools end to end: authentication (JWT), response logic, routing, escalation paths and tone, tested in staging before it sees live traffic

  • Ship daily product changes that remove ticket volume. Recent example: extending automatic refund eligibility to one-click credit purchases, accidental upgrades and month-based proration on annual terms

  • Build and maintain internal CX tooling as real software, not one-offs: scripts, jobs, dashboards, admin surfaces

  • Run QA and evals with real test suites and pass/fail rubrics, plus monitoring and alerts for outages, bugs and volume spikes

  • Own releases: staged rollouts, a regression suite before every ship, clear rollback criteria, a writeup when something reaches production

  • Build the CX reporting the org runs on: volume, deflection, CSAT, reply and resolution time, escalation accuracy, agent spend. You own the correctness and availability of the queries.

  • Build and stage the guardrails on refunds, account changes and anything touching money or PII, including the audit trail

  • Keep the knowledge base accurate and structured for the agent to parse, and manage the handoff into the ticketing system

  • Keep the CX roadmap and the coverage model current, sequenced against priorities set by the Head of CX, so gaps show up before they bite

  • Run the day-to-day with our AI platform vendor: weekly working session, joint roadmap, issues filed with reproductions

  • Carry signal across teams: Product and Engineering on bugs and rollouts, Customer Education on self-serve, community on Discord and the forums, GTM and Analytics on routing and reporting

What you’ll need

  • 5+ years in Customer Experience, Support Engineering or Support Operations, with real time spent writing code

  • You ship production code in codebases you didn't write: read TypeScript, trace logic through someone else's service, put up a PR that survives review. Our stack is TypeScript and Node.js on AWS

  • Hands-on experience building and tuning AI or LLM-powered support workflows: prompt and context engineering, routing, escalation design, evals

  • SQL experience. You own the reporting, so you shouldn't be waiting on Analytics for it

  • Code-level experience with a billing or payments API: invoices, prorations, refunds. A large share of consumer tickets live here

  • Git, PR review, CI, staging and feature flags as your default way of working

  • Real QA and eval experience: you can define rubrics, build test suites and calibrate against what good looks like

  • Judgment about where a fix belongs, in code, in the agent or in the knowledge base

  • A track record carrying signal between support, product and other functions and turning it into action

  • Comfort managing your own work in a fast-moving environment, high ownership and high autonomy

  • Genuine interest in AI, creative tools or both

What sets you apart

The most successful person in this role treats the agent and the systems around it like a product they own. They watch where it fails, ship the fix and check whether it worked. They build reporting people actually use. And they show up with improvements no one asked for yet.

For your application

During our interview process, you'll have several chances to get acquainted with the Runway product and use all the features our team has built, and that starts now. As part of your application, instead of a cover letter, we ask that you try out the Runway product, specifically build a custom workflow.

*Open to hiring remote — we also have offices in New York, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Paris, and Tel Aviv.

Runway is hiring an Infrastructure Security Engineer to secure the platform our models are trained and served on. The role covers Kubernetes platform security, cloud identity and access, software supply chain, tenant isolation in the serving layer and the research infrastructure behind our models.

Securing a company that trains and serves frontier video models is a different problem from securing a typical SaaS product. The environment includes research compute, large training datasets, a fast-moving build pipeline, and engineers who work inside AI-assisted tooling every day. jobs.descriptionHtml:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. About the role

Open to hiring remote — we also have offices in New York, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Paris, and Tel Aviv.

Runway is hiring a Detection & Response Engineer to own how we find and stop attacks against our infrastructure, our research environment and our products.

Securing a company that trains and serves frontier video models is a different problem from securing a typical SaaS product. The environment includes research compute, large training datasets, a fast-moving build pipeline and engineers who work inside AI-assisted tooling every day. Each of those changes what an attack looks like and what you need to see to catch it.

You'll join the Security team and build our detection and response program the way an engineer would: detections as code, response as automation, evidence as something you can query. This is a role with real ownership: you'll own the detection program end to end, from what we log to how quickly we close an incident. You'll report to the head of security, partner with engineers across platform and research, and shape how this function grows from here.

What you'll do

  • Own detection and response end to end: what we log, what we alert on, how we triage and how we recover

  • Write and tune detections as code across multiple cloud environments, Kubernetes, identity systems, endpoints and SaaS, and measure them on coverage and precision rather than alert volume

  • Lead incident response from the first alert through containment and forensics, then write the post-incident review people actually read

  • Build automation that takes toil out of triage, including enrichment, correlation, containment actions and evidence collection, and use LLM-based tooling where it holds up under audit

  • Monitor AI agents and developer tooling operating inside our environment, and turn that into concrete telemetry and controls

  • Partner with platform and research engineers so new systems ship with logging and response playbooks in place on day one

  • Run threat hunts and tabletop exercises against the parts of the environment that worry you most, and fix what you find

  • Turn incident and detection metrics into evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001 and enterprise customer security reviews, working with our GRC team

  • Participate in an on-call rotation for security incidents

What you'll need

  • Hands-on incident response experience: you've triaged live alerts, led investigations and written up what happened afterward

  • Experience building and tuning detections in a modern SIEM, ideally managed as code

  • Working knowledge of how attackers move through cloud and Kubernetes environments (IAM abuse, container escape, credential theft, supply chain compromise) and what that leaves behind in logs

  • Comfort writing Python, Typescript, Rust or another language to automate response work and connect security tools

  • Familiarity with at least one major cloud platform and with Kubernetes at the level of audit logs, RBAC and workload identity

  • Clear writing. Incident timelines, detection documentation and updates to leadership are all part of the job

  • Judgment about what to alert on, what to automate and when to wake someone up

Even better if you have

  • Experience monitoring GPU or HPC-style infrastructure, or research environments with large datasets

  • Experience building detections or guardrails for AI agents, LLM tooling or MCP servers

  • Cloud forensics experience: disk and memory acquisition, cloud audit trail reconstruction, chain of custody

  • Published open source detection content

We're building a creative platform used by artists, filmmakers, and teams at some of the world's most recognized brands. Our support org handles everything from a five-minute billing question to a technical escalation, and we're building out a dedicated tier for the first kind so our more experienced specialists can focus on the second.

We're looking for a Support Representative who's accurate, fast, and comfortable following a process closely under volume. No creative or AI background required. We'll train you on the product.

What you’ll do

  • Resolve high-volume, tickets across account access, billing, and plan questions for Free, Standard, and Pro and Max users

  • Use existing macros, playbooks, and AI support layer suggestions to close tickets accurately and quickly

  • Recognize when a ticket needs product judgment or creative-tool troubleshooting, and route it to Tier 2 Support or Enterprise

  • Flag recurring questions that don't have a macro yet

What you’ll need

  • Clear, accurate written communication, especially on process-driven, checklist-style work

  • Comfortable with repetitive, high-volume work without losing accuracy

  • Prior experience with tools like Zendesk, Notion, or Slack is a plus, not a requirement

  • 0-2 years in any customer-facing or process-driven role (preferably in SaaS, but not required)

  • Enough curiosity to spend a little time in the product or help docs before talking to us. No creative background needed, just evidence you looked

What sets great candidates apart

The best people in this role follow the playbook precisely and know exactly when a ticket doesn't fit it. They don't force a wrong answer to hit volume, and they don't escalate everything out of caution either. They've put in enough time with Runway to have a real sense of what it does and who uses it, so a ticket that's slightly off-script doesn't stump them, even without a creative background. When they see the same question surface three times, they ask whether it should become a macro instead of just answering it a third time.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Open to hiring remote in London, UK.

 

You will carry a book of 40-60 mid-market and emerging accounts - companies in the <$1B range, closing 25-40 deals a year at $40k-$100k and building toward larger standard deal sizes as our packaging moves upmarket. You work in a pod with a dedicated Mid-Market Engagement Manager on a shared book, with a comp plan designed to maximize earnings and customer value.

 

We are architecting the best GTM team in all of AI. If you want to grow, run fast, and sell with a leading-edge frontier AI company with room to grow your career, please apply.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Run a high-velocity full-cycle motion: 25-40 closed deals a year across inbound and outbound

  • Qualify hard and fast - your book is big, your calendar is the scarce resource, orientation to clear ROI and value orientation is a must

  • Push deal size up: committed-volume, use-case expansion plays that turn $30k starts into $100k+ repeatable motions

  • Turn product signals (usage spikes, team signups, credit burn) into pipeline

  • Work with your pod's Engagement Manager so new customers hit consumption targets and your held-back commission unlocks

 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • 3+ years of full-cycle closing experience in SaaS/AI with a quota record above 100%

  • Velocity evidence: 20+ closed deals a year, multi-channel prospecting, disciplined qualification

  • Native AI-tool fluency - you already sell with AI in your workflow, not despite it

  • Writing and demo skills strong enough to carry a deal without a solutions engineer

  • Coachability with a track record: name the coaching that changed your numbers

 

STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE

  • Sold to creative or marketing teams

  • PLG or usage-signal selling experience

  • BDR-to-AE promotion in your history - we like people who earned the chair

 

COMPENSATION

OTE $270K - $300K (50/50 base to variable). Offers equity.

We’re looking for a Senior/Staff HR Business Partner to work directly with Runway’s leaders and teams on how they grow, organize and perform. What You’ll Do

  • Partner with leaders on org design, headcount planning, team structure and leveling

  • Coach managers and executives on performance, feedback, career development and difficult conversations

  • Own complex employee relations cases from intake through resolution, including investigations, in partnership with Legal where needed

  • Work with Compensation and Talent Acquisition on offers, promotions and market adjustments

  • Use headcount, attrition, engagement and performance data to spot risks early and recommend action

  • Design and roll out programs that fit how Runway’s teams work, from manager training to engagement initiatives

  • Step in wherever the team needs it

What You’ll Need

  • 7+ years of experience in HR, including at least four as an HR Business Partner supporting fast growing teams

  • Experience at a high-growth company, ideally through periods of rapid headcount growth

  • A record of advising senior leaders and earning their trust

  • Strong employee relations experience, with sound judgment and discretion

  • Working knowledge of employment law, compensation practices and performance management frameworks

  • Clear written and verbal communication

  • Comfort operating independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment

  • A high ownership mindset and a team-first attitude

We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.

About the role

*Open to hiring remote across the US — we also have offices in New York, San Francisco, and Seattle.

We are looking for a Prototype Researcher to join Runway Labs — our research and exploration team pushing the frontier of AI video and General World Models. You’ll imagine, design, and build experimental experiences that make emerging AI capabilities tangible and communicate a compelling vision for where the technology is heading.

This role combines creative thinking, hands-on prototyping, and storytelling. You should be able to develop an original idea, build a working prototype, and shape it into a clear, memorable demonstration. Your work will help people understand new AI systems through experiences they can see, use, and engage with.

Working closely with researchers, engineers, and designers, you’ll explore new interfaces and interaction paradigms for AI-generated video, world models, and agentic systems. The focus is on research explorations that express our vision, reveal new possibilities, and strengthen Runway’s position as a full-stack research organization.

We’re looking for a motivated self-starter with strong creative judgment, technical fluency, and a portfolio that shows both what you can build and how well you can communicate an idea.

What you’ll do

  • Develop original concepts that explore the possibilities of emerging AI systems, from interactive video and world models to agentic experiences.

  • Design and build working prototypes that turn research capabilities into engaging, understandable experiences.

  • Shape each project’s story: what it explores, why it matters, and what it suggests about the future.

  • Package explorations into polished demos, films, and interactive experiences that communicate our research and vision.

  • Collaborate with researchers and engineers to understand new capabilities and identify compelling ways to demonstrate them.

  • Move quickly through experimentation, using prototypes to test ideas and refine both the experience and its narrative.

What you’ll need

  • A portfolio of original projects that demonstrates creative thinking, design craft, technical execution, and strong storytelling.

  • The ability to take an idea from an early concept to a working prototype and a compelling presentation.

  • Hands-on experience building interactive experiences with code, with the judgment to choose the right tools for each experiment.

  • Strong visual and interaction design skills, with an eye for detail and an instinct for making complex ideas accessible.

  • Genuine curiosity about AI video, world models, agentic systems, and emerging generative media.

  • Comfort working in ambiguous research environments, defining your own direction, and learning new tools as the work evolves.

  • The ability to explain the purpose and potential of your work clearly, through writing, visuals, demos, or film.

jobs.title: Pricing Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.

About the role

Preferable to have someone near an office in NYC or San Francisco, but open to hiring around the world for the right candidate.

Runway Creative is an all-in-one platform giving creators and businesses endless ways to generate and edit video, images, and audio. Our customers range from individual creators on self-serve plans to studios and enterprise marketing teams, and they generate with both Runway's own models and leading third-party models, all on one platform.

We're hiring a Pricing & Packaging Lead to own how Runway creates and captures value across all of it. You'll partner closely with our Self-Serve Product Lead to evolve our plans and credits, build the path from self-serve to enterprise, and set the pricing for every model we launch and every third-party model we serve. You'll build the pricing framework the rest of the company uses, and you'll be accountable for revenue growth, gross margin, and customer trust in equal measure.

What you’ll do

  • Own self-serve pricing & packaging: partner with the Self-Serve Product Lead on our plan ladder and credit design, including allowances, rollover, top-ups, annual vs. monthly, and regional pricing. Run a continuous program of pricing and packaging experiments with Growth and Data.

  • Build the path to enterprise: design the triggers, team and workspace constructs, seat and credit-pool models, and commit and consumption contracts that move customers from self-serve to enterprise. Equip Sales with pricing playbooks, discount bands, and deal guardrails.

  • Create a company-wide pricing framework: publish Runway's pricing principles, value metrics, and decision process so any product team can price new features and products with confidence. Run a regular pricing council with Product, Finance, Research, and GTM.

  • Price our models: set launch pricing for every Runway model release, working with Research and Infrastructure on cost-to-serve. Define how model pricing evolves from launch through deprecation as inference costs change.

  • Own third-party model economics: set credit pricing and target margins for the partner models we serve, monitor competitive pricing, and work with Partnerships on vendor terms. Make per-model margin visible to the whole company.

  • Keep pricing changes trustworthy: own how we communicate every pricing change, from advance notice and in-product usage visibility to spend controls and customer FAQs. Changes should land as clearly as they were designed.

  • Build the team: hire and lead a small pricing team over time, and partner closely with billing engineering to turn decisions into systems.

What you’ll need

  • 10+ years across pricing, monetization, strategy, or strategic finance, with 5+ years directly owning pricing and packaging decisions. A track record of moving revenue, conversion, and margin, not just producing recommendations.

  • Deep experience with usage, credit, or consumption-based pricing. You can build a cost-to-serve and margin model from compute and inference inputs, and you understand how hybrid seat + usage models behave in the wild.

  • Experience across self-serve and sales-led motions. You've shipped pricing changes for PLG subscription products and designed the contracts and guardrails that support enterprise expansion.

  • Rigorous and experimental. You're fluent in pricing experiments, willingness-to-pay research, and cohort analysis, and comfortable in SQL and financial models.

  • You thrive in an environment with rapid pace and a high accountability culture. You make decisions with incomplete information and know when a pricing call needs more data and when it needs to ship.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication. You can drive a decision across Product, Finance, Research, and Sales, and explain a pricing change to customers in a way that builds trust.

  • Bonus: pricing experience at an AI lab, AI-native product, API or developer platform, or creative tools company; experience pricing third-party or marketplace offerings.

Runway strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on competitive market rates for our size, stage and industry, and salary is just one part of the overall compensation package we provide.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level and qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. The range shared below is a general expectation for the function as posted, but we are also open to considering candidates who may be more or less experienced than outlined in the job description. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

Lastly, the provided range is the expected salary for candidates in the U.S. Outside of those regions, there may be a change in the range, which again, will be communicated to candidates.

Working at Runway

Great things come from great teams. We’d love to hear from you.

We’re committed to creating a space where our employees can bring their full selves to work and have equal opportunity to succeed. So regardless of race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, origin, ability, age, veteran status, if joining this mission speaks to you, we encourage you to apply.

We’re looking for a Senior HR Generalist to own the day-to-day of Runway’s HR function and shape how it scales. You’ll work directly with the HR Manager as a strategic partner, and you’ll have the autonomy to make decisions, set priorities and fix what’s broken without waiting to be asked.

What you’ll do

  • Own the employee lifecycle from onboarding through offboarding for full-time employees and contractors, and keep improving the process as the team grows

  • Own HRIS administration and data integrity in Rippling, including reporting, audits and workflow automation

  • Manage employee visa and immigration processes in partnership with outside counsel

  • Oversee leave administration and accommodations across jurisdictions, and keep policies and practices compliant with current employment law

  • Run key programs end to end with the HR Manager, including performance reviews, open enrollment, engagement surveys and compensation cycles

  • Act as the go-to resource for employees and managers on benefits, policies and HR processes

  • Identify gaps in HR operations and ship fixes: updated policies, clearer documentation and more efficient tooling

  • Pitch in wherever the team needs; no task is too small if it moves things forward

What you’ll need

  • 5+ years of experience in an HR Generalist or people operations role at a high-growth company

  • Deep working knowledge of benefits, leave administration, immigration basics and employment law across multiple states

  • Experience running company-wide programs such as performance cycles, open enrollment and engagement surveys

  • Strong HRIS skills, with Rippling experience a strong plus

  • Clear written and verbal communication, and the credibility to advise managers and senior leaders

  • Comfort operating independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment

  • Exceptional organization and attention to detail

  • A high ownership mindset and a team-first attitude

About the role

*Open to hiring remote across North America — we also have offices in NYC, London, San Francisco, Paris and Seattle.

We’re looking for a Creative with a focus on campaigns for Product Marketing. This is not a growth role. It’s a hands-on campaign creative role for someone who makes the work themselves, with AI as their primary medium. You’ll own full-funnel launch campaigns for Runway’s products, features and research: launch films, key visuals, landing pages, lifecycle emails, onboarding flows and everything in between. You’ll report to the Creative Director of Product Marketing.

We’re open to creatives who lead with art direction or with copy. What matters is that you make the work yourself and can move across both. Your work will directly shape how people discover, understand and adopt what Runway builds. That means work with real taste that stops people mid-scroll, makes new research feel tangible, and turns curiosity into first use. You’ll also help build the workflows and automations that let a small team ship at the pace of the product. You’ll partner closely with product marketing, design, research, growth and product teams.

What you’ll do

  • Build full-funnel launch campaigns end to end: the idea, the script, the boards, the generation, the edit, the finish.

  • Make launch films, key visuals and campaign systems that hold up next to the best brand work in the world.

  • Turn research breakthroughs into work people outside the field can feel, not just read about.

  • Extend each campaign across every surface (landing pages, social, email, in-product) without losing the idea.

  • Work at the pace of the product: several launches at once, fast timelines, quality never optional.

  • Build the machine behind the work. Turn what you make into reusable prompts, workflows and automated pipelines, so every campaign starts further ahead than the last.

  • Treat every new model as new creative territory, and show the team what’s now possible before anyone asks.

What you’ll need

  • 4+ years making creative at an agency, studio or brand, with real campaigns shipped for real clients.

  • A portfolio that proves taste first. AI-generated or AI-assisted work should be central to it.

  • Fluency with image and video models, plus the craft tools to finish (editing, compositing, design).

  • Art direction instincts: casting, styling, light, composition, type and pacing.

  • A strong lead discipline (art direction, motion/edit or copy) and comfort across the others.

  • A builder’s mindset. You’ve chained tools together, automated the repetitive parts, or built workflows others use.

  • The range to move from a cinematic launch film to a single perfect frame in the same week.

Bonus points

  • Experience launching creative tools, AI products or research.

  • You’ve already built something interesting on Runway.

  • Experience providing practical recommendations to senior leaders with limited time and information

  • Sound judgment in ambiguity: track record of gathering key information quickly and helping the business make smart decisions

  • Deep sense of ownership, whether you're advising our CEO on a novel legal issue or testing your new AI-enabled workflow for the nth time

  • J.D. and admission in good standing with at least one state bar

  • Experience closing strategic, IP-heavy partnerships

  • Experience in B2C and B2B industries and in product-led and enterprise businesses

  • Experience closing B2B SaaS customer deals

jobs.descriptionHtml:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.

About the role

Runway’s Legal team is looking for a Litigation Counsel to help manage Runway’s litigation and dispute resolution work day-to-day, with strategic guidance from the Associate General Counsel, Litigation. You’ll work on a broad docket of litigation and pre-litigation matters, advise business stakeholders on litigation risk, and help to build out the litigation function as the business scales. You’ll join a lean team where everyone carries real responsibility, and you may have the opportunity to pitch in on a variety of other legal domains to support the team.

You’ll work at the cutting edge of a highly technical and rapidly evolving area of the law, navigating challenges that are shaping the future of the industry. This role reports to the Associate General Counsel, Litigation.

What you’ll do

  • Manage litigation, third-party process, dispute resolution, and regulatory requests involving the company. This spans everything from helping Runway develop its strategy on cutting-edge legal questions to owning all in-house-side discovery execution

  • Manage outside counsel across all stages of litigation, with a focus on case strategy and the quality of written advocacy

  • Build, improve, document, and execute repeatable processes for the areas above to help the litigation function operate efficiently and effectively at scale

  • Advise key stakeholders on litigation risk, aligning legal strategy with business priorities

  • Field day-to-day requests from legal team members and cross-functional partners who want your litigation perspective on their commercial, product, and other legal work

  • Partner with Runway’s Customer Support Team to advise on and help resolve small disputes and escalations

  • Monitor regulatory and policy developments relating to generative AI, and advise our AI safety, product, and engineering teams on them as appropriate

  • Dive into the technical aspects of the product and industry to learn them inside and out, and use that knowledge to inform your advice to the business

  • Support the team in other legal domains, which may include employment, trust & safety, policy, commercial, privacy, and IP

What you'll need

  • A J.D. and admission in good standing with at least one state bar

  • 5+ years of dedicated litigation experience (can include clerkships)

  • Litigation experience in some combination of copyright, class action, securities, and regulatory matters

  • Deep knowledge of complex civil litigation practice and procedure, including discovery and federal and state court rules

  • A track record of running litigation matters, including developing case strategy, managing discovery, drafting and editing briefs, gathering information efficiently and preparing witnesses for depositions

  • A working knowledge of the key legal issues in Runway’s industry

  • Excellent written and oral communication skills. This includes giving practical, clear, and commercially sensible advice, and advocating for a position while staying open-minded

  • Sound judgment under pressure and strong business acumen

  • The ability to manage multiple workstreams, prioritize effectively, and consistently deliver results

  • A strong sense of ownership, both in the highest-level strategic work and in smaller day-to-day tasks

  • Creative problem-solving, low ego, curiosity, and a bias for action

Nice to have

  • In-house experience (particularly at a technology company)

  • Experience with emerging technologies, particularly generative AI and copyright litigation

  • Familiarity with Runway and the generative AI video industry

  • Excitement about generative AI, and the motivation to become a leading expert in the legal landscape governing a rapidly innovating industry

We're looking for a Social Media Lead to build the strategy and operating model behind how Runway shows up on social. Our audience spans filmmakers, artists, developers, researchers and enterprise teams, and each of them comes to our channels for something different. Your job is to give every channel a clear role and make sure our biggest moments, from model launches and research releases to film festivals and conferences, land with real distribution behind them.

You'll bring a strong point of view on where Runway should show up and how. You'll help our researchers, engineers, creatives and executives share the work closest to them with credibility and authenticity, and you'll treat our community of creators as collaborators in telling the story. You'll be hands-on where it matters, but this role is defined by strategic leadership and operational ownership.

What you’ll do

  • Set Runway's social strategy, raise the creative bar and build the calendar around a steady, always-on presence that leads into our biggest launches

  • Define a distinct role for each channel across X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn and emerging community platforms

  • Decide when Runway, a researcher, an executive, a creator, a customer or a partner should lead the story, then build the distribution plan around it

  • Partner with Research, Product, Comms and Brand to turn model launches, research papers and product updates into native, credible social moments

  • Help Runway researchers, engineers and executives post about their work, with clear guidance, coaching and coordinated amplification

  • Work with our Community team, partners and our broader creator community to put the work made with Runway at the center of our channels

  • Establish a clear scorecard and use social insights to sharpen the work over time

What success looks like

  • Social runs on data-driven goals across reach, awareness, demand, campaign lift and audience insight

  • Runway has a clear social point of view and a defined role for each channel

  • Social is a strategic driver of visibility, creative adoption and demand, not an internal posting service

  • Runway's researchers, engineers and executives have an easy, trusted way to share their work, and the strongest posts get coordinated amplification

  • Creators see Runway's channels as the best place for their work to be seen

What you’ll need

  • 5+ years of experience in strategic social or related marketing programs; 2+ years at a top-tier technology, consumer, media or entertainment company is a plus

  • A track record of building social strategy and the operating model behind it: prioritization, agency and contractor management, workflows, measurement and executive alignment

  • Excellent editorial judgment and an instinct for what feels credible and native on each platform, especially X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and LinkedIn

  • Fluency across disparate cultures: film, art and creators, AI and startups, venture capital and Silicon Valley; comfort translating technical research for a broad audience

  • Comfort with performance and brand measurement, including how to separate correlation from impact and how to run disciplined tests

  • Hands-on familiarity with generative AI tools, including Runway, and curiosity about where they're headed

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-moving environment where priorities shift with each launch

We're looking for a Social Media Lead to build the strategy and operating model behind how Runway shows up on social. Our audience spans filmmakers, artists, developers, researchers and enterprise teams, and each of them comes to our channels for something different. jobs.descriptionHtml:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.

About the role

*Open to hiring in the US.

We're building a creative platform used by artists, filmmakers, and teams at some of the world's most recognized brands. Our support org handles everything from a five-minute billing question to a technical escalation, and we're building out a dedicated tier for the first kind so our more experienced specialists can focus on the second.

We're looking for a Support Representative who's accurate, fast, and comfortable following a process closely under volume. No creative or AI background required. We'll train you on the product.

What you’ll do

  • Resolve high-volume, tickets across account access, billing, and plan questions for Free, Standard, and Pro and Max users

  • Use existing macros, playbooks, and AI support layer suggestions to close tickets accurately and quickly

  • Recognize when a ticket needs product judgment or creative-tool troubleshooting, and route it to Tier 2 Support or Enterprise

  • Flag recurring questions that don't have a macro yet

What you’ll need

  • Clear, accurate written communication, especially on process-driven, checklist-style work

  • Comfortable with repetitive, high-volume work without losing accuracy

  • Prior experience with tools like Zendesk, Notion, or Slack is a plus, not a requirement

  • 0-2 years in any customer-facing or process-driven role (preferably in SaaS, but not required)

  • Enough curiosity to spend a little time in the product or help docs before talking to us. No creative background needed, just evidence you looked

What sets great candidates apart

The best people in this role follow the playbook precisely and know exactly when a ticket doesn't fit it. They don't force a wrong answer to hit volume, and they don't escalate everything out of caution either. They've put in enough time with Runway to have a real sense of what it does and who uses it, so a ticket that's slightly off-script doesn't stump them, even without a creative background. When they see the same question surface three times, they ask whether it should become a macro instead of just answering it a third time.

We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. *Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.

About the role

Preferable to have someone near one of our offices in NYC or San Francisco.

Runway’s Commercial Counsel Fellowship is an intensive, full-time, 1 year venture dedicated to fostering high caliber early-career lawyers who want to build real in-house experience at a fast-moving AI company. You'll work directly alongside our Commercial Counsel team on live deals from your first weeks, with hands-on training and mentorship along the way.

No prior commercial or in-house experience is required. We care more about sharp judgment, strong writing, and a fast learning curve than a specific background. Comfort working in a highly technical, rapidly evolving area of the law is a must. Whether you're coming from a law firm, a clerkship, or straight out of law school, we'll teach you how to negotiate commercial agreements and partner with the business.

 

What you'll do

  • Draft, review, and negotiate Runway's commercial agreements, including B2B SaaS customer contracts for our generative AI platform and APIs, DPAs, partnership agreements, and vendor agreements, taking on more complex deals as you ramp

  • Partner with the sales team with fast, practical answers that help close deals

  • Help scale and automate our commercial processes and tools, including templates, playbooks, contract review automation, and our legal tech stack

  • Learn the technical side of our generative AI products inside and out, so your advice to the business is grounded in how they work

  • Research and track technical, legal, and policy developments in generative AI, and share what matters with the team

  • Depending on your interests, contribute to projects across the broader legal team, such as privacy, IP, product counseling, or compliance

 

What you'll get

  • Hands-on training in commercial contracting and in-house practice, with real ownership from early on

  • Mentorship from experienced in-house lawyers, with regular feedback on your work

  • Exposure to cross-functional teams across sales, partnerships, product, and marketing, and to the Runway Executive Team

  • A front-row seat to the legal questions shaping generative AI video

  • Potential to convert to a full-time role at the end of the fellowship, in Commercial Counsel or another area of the legal team

 

What you'll need

  • A J.D. plus admission in good standing with at least one state bar (or sitting for the bar before the fellowship starts)

  • 0–3 years of legal experience, for example at a law firm, in a clerkship, in an in-house or government role

  • A strong academic record and excellent legal writing and analytical skills

  • Bias for action and a willingness to take ownership

  • Growth mindset and an eagerness to learn quickly, take feedback, and improve how things get done

  • Clear, practical communication with non-lawyers

  • Operational mindset

  • Excitement about generative AI and motivation to continuously learn more about the legal landscape governing a new and exciting industry

 

Nice to have

  • Exposure to technology transactions, SaaS agreements, IP, or data privacy, through practice, coursework, a clinic, or a summer associate role

  • Experience using AI tools in your own legal work

  • Familiarity with how AI or software products are built

FAQs

  • Are there specific fellowship start dates or can I start anytime?

    • We do not currently have specific start dates. Start dates can be year round.

  • I am 10 years out of law school. Can I still apply for the fellowship?

    • The fellowship is meant for early-career lawyers (first 3 years of legal practice). However, lots of lawyers take different, non-traditional paths. If you are an experienced lawyer who is early in your commercial counsel career, you are still welcome to apply. Explain your career transition and interest in commercial legal work in your application.
